output.reason: A few days of right-hand numbness and tingling worse at night, with reported absence of weakness, facial droop or speech change, fits a common nerve-compression pattern manageable with self-care guidance and a clear escalation trigger.
output.patientMessage: You can start self-care now: avoid bending the wrist while sleeping (a neutral wrist splint helps), take breaks from repetitive hand use, and shake the hand out when symptoms wake you. Night-worse hand tingling is often nerve compression at the wrist. Call 911 if sudden weakness, face droop or slurred speech appears. Message a Counsel clinician if numbness persists beyond a few weeks, spreads, or hand weakness or dropping objects develops.
differential: Median nerve compression at the wrist (carpal tunnel syndrome)
Other peripheral nerve or cervical nerve root irritation

redFlags.concern: Recent trauma or swollen, painful, tense forearm/hand
